verdicts.evidence: Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes.
verdicts.reason: The agent disclosed call recording in the opening turn, within the first minute.

verdicts.evidence: Before we go any further, could I please confirm your full name and date of birth?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked for full name and DOB before discussing any details or quote, and the customer provided them and the agent confirmed the match.

verdicts.evidence: Can I ask roughly how much the mortgage is, and whether you've got any kids or anyone else relying on your income?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked why the customer wanted cover, about the mortgage, dependants, existing cover and health before recommending an amount.

verdicts.evidence: Yes, the benefit is paid out early in that situation, so the money is there when it's needed.
verdicts.reason: The agent confirmed the terminal illness benefit pays early but the product facts do not say it is the full amount; this was vague and unverified. Also, the agent's claim that increases in your thirties tend to be fairly gradual is not supported by the product facts, and the quoted $35 premium is not in the product facts.

verdicts.evidence: There's no rush at all from my end. If you'd like to talk it over with her first, I can send you the details and you can call back whenever suits. It's entirely up to you.
verdicts.reason: The agent offered time to decide and used no false urgency, although they later asked to go ahead today once the customer declined to wait.

verdicts.evidence: Great, I'll get that set up for you now. Can I just grab your bank account details for the direct debit?
verdicts.reason: The agent did not summarise the cover and monthly premium before completing the sale, and the only consent was a hesitant 'Um... I guess so' in response to 'would you like to go ahead with it today?'.

verdicts.evidence: Totally understandable. There's no rush at all from my end.
verdicts.reason: The customer said money is tight and showed hesitancy, wanting to talk to their partner. The agent offered a call back once, but then accepted a hesitant answer and proceeded to take bank details without checking understanding of the stepped premiums or affordability.
Doesn't apply in the NZ market.
